analysis: This 70-74-year-old male with ECOG 1 and smoking history developed severe neutropenia (grade 4) early, suggesting significant bone marrow suppression from therapy. Subsequent cough, dyspnea, and fatigue (grade 2) indicate possible pulmonary or infectious complication. Supraventricular extrasystoles may reflect cardiac stress. Multi-organ involvement (hematologic, pulmonary, cardiac) and incomplete recovery of arrhythmia suggest moderate mortality risk, though no progressive organ failure yet.
